   Everything Jensen Huang said about China is out the window
 Huang spent years warning that China could win the AI race, and that export controls on cutting-edge chips have backfired. 
 Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox
 Across Asia, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s techno-optimism that AI shouldn’t be another zero-sum game was infectious, the writer says.
 PHOTO: REUTERS
 Catherine Thorbecke
 Published   Nov 10, 2026, 09:05 AM
 Updated   Nov 10, 2026, 09:33 AM
 Set as preferred source Unlock audio No American argued harder for selling artificial-intelligence chips to China than Nvidia’s chief executive Jensen Huang. His recurring advocacy previously could be easily explained by run-of-the-mill self-interest, with billions of dollars at stake. Now, that explanation has suddenly become a lot murkier.
 Whether he was wrong or right in what he believed, everything that Huang has spent nearly every public appearance pitching in recent years has gone out the window after reports that he had an affair with a woman US intelligence officials suspect of being a Chinese spy .
